item.title: Gone Girl, 2014 - ★★★★★
item.description:
“Nick:
You fucking cunt!

Amy:
I'm the cunt you married. The only time you liked yourself was when you were trying to be someone this cunt might like. I'm not a quitter, I'm that cunt. I killed for you; who else can say that? You think you'd be happy with a nice Midwestern girl? No way, baby! I'm it.

Nick:
Fuck. You're delusional. I mean, you're insane, why would you even want this? Yes, I loved you and then all we did was resent each other, try to control each other. We caused each other pain.

Amy:
That's marriage.”

Both of these people are crazy as fuck lmao. I haven’t read the book but I know that Nick isn’t made out to be a piece of shit in the movie like he really is in the book. Anyway, third rewatch I still love this film. Nothing will ever be as crazy as the first time I watched it though… so intense and thrilling. Still great though and I love picking up new things or just seeing old things I love about it.

Peace and Love

item.title: Casablanca, 1942 - ★★★★½
item.description:
I really enjoyed Casablanca. A lot of people say this and Citizen Kane are the best films ever. I would have to disagree with that statement, but with that being said I enjoyed this a lot more than Citizen Kane. Bogart’s acting can get a little annoying sometimes (in general with all his movies) but he still put on a good performance here as well as everyone else. I enjoyed watching this movie a lot and it’s also great from a technical aspect. It’s been a few days so my review isn’t as detailed as I’d like it to be. I’m happy to watch more movies of classic cinema and I haven’t watched movies fr in a year so it’s really nice to jump back in. 

Peace and Love

item.title: Spider-Man: No Way Home, 2021 - ★★★★
item.description:
I’ll give it 4 for now but my worry with this movie is that it only hits in the theater because of nostalgia and hype just like Endgame, and then overtime people realize the movie isn’t all that good. However, I’ll put that aside for now and put aside my problems with the film and first act because I had a fun time watching it and loved seeing Tobey, Andrew, Dafoe, and Molina on screen even if it was fan service. I’m curious to see what they do with the multiverse now that it’s canon, and I’m glad Peter finally has a good setup for good Spiderman movies focused on him and not Tony and the rest of the MCU.
